item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00280","case1_error":"Inserts $3,000 in taxes without calculation or justification; 20% of the $5,000 pretax profit is $1,000.","case2_error":"Treats monthly materials costs as per-vehicle costs, multiplying those expenses by production quantities.","reason":"The first substitutes an unsupported tax amount; the second explicitly misinterprets aggregate costs as unit costs.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00281","case1_error":"Constructs incorrect population ratios, using 2/19 beavers per human and then inverting that to obtain moose per human.","case2_error":"Omits the front-yard nest's four eggs, summing only 10 and 3.","reason":"Incorrect ratio construction differs from omitting an entire additive quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00282","case1_error":"Uses one bottle's 80-load capacity as the total capacity of two bottles.","case2_error":"Misreads 18 remaining watermelons as sold, then adds monetary earnings and profit to produce a watermelon count.","reason":"Failure to scale capacity by bottle count differs from confusing inventory status and equating money with item counts.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00283","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written calorie sum as 2,175 instead of 1,975.","case2_error":"Treats the one-cent payment per page as payment per book, omitting the 150-page conversion.","reason":"The first is numerical evaluation of a correct expression; the second uses an incorrect payment-per-book relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00284","case1_error":"Provides 6,186 after correct formulas without showing any calculation supporting that final number; the formulas yield 859.","case2_error":"Treats monthly materials costs as per-vehicle costs, multiplying those expenses by production quantities.","reason":"An unsupported final number following correct formulas differs from an explicit erroneous cost relation.","judgment":"different"}]}
